verdict.rationale: Pipecat's own interruptions docs say that when the user barges in, the bot stops immediately, in-flight work is cancelled, and the pipeline is ready for new input. That covers stopping speech and recovering the turn, and Krisp noise filtering further reduces false interruptions. The docs never say how conversation context is updated after an interruption, such as truncating the unspoken assistant reply, so coverage is partial. Missing for 10: documentation of context updating on interruption, configurable interruption strategies, and independent hands-on corroboration of barge-in quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the agent to handle interruptions (barge-in) gracefully — stopping speech, updating context, and recovering the turn

citations.quote: Interruptions (also called barge-in) let the user talk over the bot. When the user starts speaking while the bot is talking, the bot stops immediately, in-flight work is cancelled
the pipeline is ready for the new user input
Eliminates background noise and voices that cause false interruptions, powered by Krisp.
